status: Exploratory event/state applications proposed after previous stock-comparison analyses; not preregistered confirmatory evidence
question: Which fixed risk modules change distribution across historical market stages, and do observed changes accompany greater joint downside exposure?
observation: Daily vector of the same fixed asset coordinates within each module, retained across phases; no stock sorting or cross-stock averaging in the test
primary_representation: Estimated standardized GARCH residual vector, with a single pre-event fitted filter per coordinate shared by all phases
raw_returns: Descriptive downside and market-path analysis only

China2015.note: User selected three historical stages. June 12 is a retrospective market peak, not a real-time trading signal or exogenous treatment. Unequal phase counts are retained.

China2024.note: A policy-announcement comparison, not a presumption of a permanent bull/bear transition or causal policy effect. Reuses the historical cohort for transparent scope; not the entire 2024 industry universe.

US2020.note: Independent overseas illustration around the Federal Reserve policy announcement in the pandemic context. Latest-vintage public industry-portfolio returns, not a point-in-time investment backtest.

China_selection: Within cached, independently preselected 2014 cohort: descending 2014 CSI300 weight in each historical industry, ties by identifier. No event-period return or survival screen. Missing observations retained on the original calendar; insufficient modules reported, not replaced.
US_source: Kenneth French 49 Industry Portfolios, daily value-weighted returns; historical SIC membership is maintained by the source
within_phase_split: First floor(0.40*N_calendar) dates fit classifiers, next five dates buffer, remaining dates test. Apply complete-coordinate masks after defining the split; do not compress missing dates. Minimum 12 complete vectors in both classifier-fit and test per phase.
multiplicity: Holm across the full planned 15 event-module tests separately for each method; nonestimable tests count conservatively as 1 for adjustment but remain missing in reported estimates
downside_diagnostic: For each coordinate, baseline-only 5th percentile of raw daily log return. Record the fraction of phase days on which at least half of coordinates fall below those fixed thresholds. This is a descriptive joint-downside statistic, not an independently validated selection outcome.
no_claims: a smaller p-value means greater damage
existing calibration failures are solved by changing events
